title: Integer-shift coherence for a prescribed pair-category functor
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and noetherian finite-dimensional schemes $T,S$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. For $H=T,S$, use the finite-stage categories $\mathcal C_E(H)$ and pair category $\mathcal P_H$ of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category], with their canonical integer shifts and inclusion functors $j_E^H$ from [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus]. Write $\sigma^H_{F/E,n,K}:T^H_{F/E}(K[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}(T^H_{F/E}K)[n]$ for the iterated scalar shift comparisons of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. Use the meaning of exact functor from [def-weil-triangulated-category].

Let $\Phi_E:\mathcal C_E(T)\to\mathcal C_E(S)$ be additive functors [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor] equipped with natural isomorphisms $s_{E,n,K}:\Phi_E(K[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}(\Phi_EK)[n]$ for every $n\in\mathbf Z$, satisfying the zero and addition coherence equations. Let $\beta_{F/E}:T^S_{F/E}\Phi_E\xrightarrow{\sim}\Phi_F T^T_{F/E}$ be natural isomorphisms satisfying $\beta_{E/E}=1$ and
$$\beta_{G/E,K}\circ a^S_{G,F,E,\Phi_EK}=\Phi_G(a^T_{G,F,E,K})\circ\beta_{G/F,T^T_{F/E}K}\circ T^S_{G/F}(\beta_{F/E,K})$$
for $E\subseteq F\subseteq G$. Suppose, for every $E\subseteq F$, $n$ and $K$, that
$$s_{F,n,T^T_{F/E}K}\circ\Phi_F(\sigma^T_{F/E,n,K})\circ\beta_{F/E,K[n]}=(\beta_{F/E,K})[n]\circ\sigma^S_{F/E,n,\Phi_EK}\circ T^S_{F/E}(s_{E,n,K}).$$
Let $G:\mathcal P_T\to\mathcal P_S$ be an additive functor with object formula $G(E,K)=(E,\Phi_EK)$ and representative formula
$$G[M,u]=[M,\beta_{M/F,L}^{-1}\circ\Phi_M(u)\circ\beta_{M/E,K}]$$
for $u:T^T_{M/E}K\to T^T_{M/F}L$.

Then $s_{n,(E,K)}=[E,s_{E,n,K}]$ are the components of natural isomorphisms $s_n:G(-[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}(G-)[n]$. They satisfy the zero and addition coherence equations. Explicitly, for categories $\mathcal A=\mathcal P_T$, $\mathcal B=\mathcal P_S$, write $z^H_X:X[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}X$ and $c^H_{n,m,X}:X[n+m]\xrightarrow{\sim}(X[n])[m]$ for the canonical shift identifications, where $H=\mathcal A,\mathcal B$. Then
$$s_{0,X}=(z^{\mathcal B}_{GX})^{-1}\circ G(z^{\mathcal A}_X),$$
$$s_{n+m,X}=(c^{\mathcal B}_{n,m,GX})^{-1}\circ(s_{n,X})[m]\circ s_{m,X[n]}\circ G(c^{\mathcal A}_{n,m,X}).$$
Moreover there is a natural isomorphism $\kappa_E:Gj_E^T\xrightarrow{\sim}j_E^S\Phi_E$ with identity components. It is compatible with these shift comparisons: if $s^{Gj_E^T}$ and $s^{j_E^S\Phi_E}$ denote the composite shift comparisons, then
$$s^{j_E^S\Phi_E}_{n,K}\circ\kappa_{E,K[n]}=(\kappa_{E,K})[n]\circ s^{Gj_E^T}_{n,K}.$$
No preservation of distinguished triangles by $G$ is assumed or concluded.

source.place: Proof, exactness sentence; the shift-compatibility argument is written out by NP from the finite-stage comparisons. Compare lean/Sheaf/Paper/PbcDescentFunctors.lean:172-273, shiftHom, shiftIso, descendedCommShift and inclusionComp_commShift.

mathlib_searches.query: Coherent functors on finite coefficient stage pair categories inherit natural integer shift comparisons compatible with zero and addition and stage inclusions
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits: HasShift.Induced.add, HasShift.induced, Functor.ShiftSequence.induced_shiftMap, SingleFunctors.shiftIso, Functor.ShiftSequence.induced, Functor.ShiftSequence, shiftFunctor_of_induced, ShiftMkCore.add. These construct shifts or shift sequences, not the stage-pair descent and its inclusion compatibility.
No hits in Mathlib/CategoryTheory for stage systems, pair categories or descended CommShift.

mathlib_searches.query: Descent of coherent shift isomorphisms to a filtered pair category with zero and addition coherence and shift compatible inclusion comparisons
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits: Pseudofunctor.DescentData.isoMk, Functor.ShiftSequence.induced.isoZero, ShiftMkCore.mk, TwistShiftData.shiftMkCore, Functor.CommShift.ofHasShiftOfFullyFaithful, Functor.FullyFaithful.hasShift, ShiftMkCore.zero, HasShift.induced. Fully faithful shift transfer and induced shifts do not apply to an arbitrary descended functor between already fixed pair-category shifts.

Twelve hits: NatTrans.CommShift.id, isoRefl_hom, CommShift, Functor.CommShift.ofIso_compatibility, NatTrans.CommShift.of_core, leftUnitor, rightUnitor, of_iso_inv, of_iso_symm, of_isIso, Functor.CommShift.ofComp_compatibility, NatTrans.CommShift.comp. These are the definition and formal operations, not the stage-pair coherence theorem.

mathlib_searches.query: A functor induced by a morphism of directed category systems commutes with integer shifts when each stage functor and comparison natural isomorphism commutes coherently with shifts
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits: Functor.ShiftSequence.induced_shiftMap, shiftFunctor_of_induced, Functor.shiftMap, Functor.ShiftSequence.induced, induced.shiftIso, Functor.CommShift.ofInduced, Functor.map_shiftFunctorComm, induced.shiftIso_hom_app_obj. Induced-shift constructions assume a different universal situation; none gives this pair-category statement.

Eight hits in Shift: Adjunction.lean:208, CommShift.lean:147,346,488,503,505, CommShiftTwo.lean:84,173. Read CommShift.lean:138-169 and 470-507 and Induced.lean:20-135. The class specifies precisely the zero/add laws; ofHasShiftOfFullyFaithful assumes a fully faithful functor and changes the source shift, while Induced assumes fully faithful precomposition. Neither is this lemma.
